correctness.rationale: The complete known finite population of 864 three-dimensional all-smooth ternary cubic spaces is independently reproduced by exact Gröbner smoothness and row-echelon enumeration. All 168 projective coordinate changes partition the population into eight orbits. Exact projective-chart Gröbner elimination shows the base ideal is the unit ideal for six orbit representatives, and for exactly two size-eight representatives is generated in X=1 by Y+h(Z) and (Z^3+Z^2+1)^2, with no points at X=0. The irreducible degree-three factor gives geometric base length six, supported on a Frobenius orbit of three doubled points. Orbit propagation proves 16 exceptional and 848 basepoint-free nets; the latter define finite maps of degree nine by ampleness and intersection theory.

value.rationale: The exact geometric base ideal is a central invariant of any linear system: it decides whether the three cubics define a morphism and, if so, its degree. Among the natural maximum-dimensional all-smooth binary systems, exactly 848 produce finite maps of degree nine and exactly 16 have a doubled closed degree-three base scheme. This is more than restatement of the old orbit count or rational base-point statistics; it identifies nonrational nilpotent base structure by new exact elimination.
